metadata.title: IT/OT Integration: Shop Floor to Enterprise
metadata.author: SnapLogic Solutions Engineering

content.title: IT/OT Integration: Shop Floor to Enterprise
content.content:
Modern aerospace manufacturing generates massive volumes of operational data from PLM systems (design, engineering BOMs), MES platforms (production execution, quality control, traceability), and OT systems (SCADA, sensors, industrial equipment). This data is typically siloed — inaccessible to ERP and business intelligence tools.

**PLM to Manufacturing BOM (Engineering BOM to Manufacturing BOM)**: Engineering releases a new component or change order in PLM. That change must propagate to the ERP manufacturing BOM before production can consume it. Without integration this is a manual, error-prone handoff — a primary source of production delays and rework. SnapLogic automates this synchronisation bidirectionally, with transformation logic to handle structural differences between engineering and manufacturing BOMs.

**ERP to MES (Production order release)**: ERP creates a production order. MES must receive it with the correct routing, materials list, and work instructions before the shop floor can execute. SnapLogic handles the translation between ERP's planning data model and MES's execution data model — including routing structures, operation sequences, and component allocations that differ significantly between systems.

**MES to ERP (Actuals confirmation)**: As production progresses, MES generates actuals: quantities completed, materials consumed, labour booked, non-conformances raised. These must flow back to ERP in real time for accurate costing, inventory management, and delivery forecasting. This is high-volume, time-sensitive data — exactly the workload SnapLogic Ultra-Pipelines are designed for.

**PLM and MES (Work instructions and quality records)**: MES needs current work instructions from PLM to display at the workstation. Quality records and non-conformance data generated in MES must link back to the PLM revision that was active at time of production — essential for aerospace traceability and AS9100 compliance.

**Key message**: API-first integration platforms excel at application connectivity and API lifecycle management. They are not designed for high-volume, schema-heavy data integration between PLM, MES, and ERP. SnapLogic fills exactly this gap — as the data integration layer that sits alongside the existing API platform, not as a replacement.
